title: Communicate a Tradeoff

answers: Choose a candidate, state the accepted cost and name evidence that would change the choice.
List many implementation features without tying them to user constraints.
Claim the faster asymptotic bound settles latency at every input size.
writing.exampleCaption: The enum only records the two options; your answer still has to name the facts that pick one.
writing.explanation:
A senior answer does not call one tool universally best. Name the current constraint, compare at least two viable choices, state the cost you accept, and say what evidence would change the decision.

A tradeoff answer begins with the constraint that matters now. For a mobile Rust editor, local compilation may improve privacy and offline capability while consuming more device resources and supporting a narrower toolchain target. A server compiler may support more crates but introduce network dependence and operational cost. Neither is universally superior. State which users and failure modes the current design serves, and which cost you are accepting.

Compare at least two viable options on the same dimensions: correctness, latency, memory, maintenance, security boundary, and reversibility. Avoid a table of generic advantages that does not change a decision. If p95 latency is the requirement, define its measurement. If offline use matters, define which operations must work offline. If privacy is the requirement, identify exactly what data crosses a network boundary. A constraint becomes useful only when it can be observed or tested.

In an interview, make a provisional recommendation and name the evidence that would change it. 'I would start with option A because our workloads are small; if production traces show queue age above two seconds, I would revisit B' is stronger than claiming A is best. Mention migration cost if the choice becomes difficult to reverse. Clear communication is not certainty; it is a decision that another engineer can inspect, challenge, and update.

Interview follow-up: What metric would reveal that your chosen queue capacity harms tail latency? How would you gather that evidence?
writing.feedback: A useful recommendation states constraints, alternatives, a measurable outcome and the condition for revisiting it.
